raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With `disable_chunked_mm_input`, the scheduler still splits a multimodal item when a prefix cache hit ends inside it and the step has no room for the rest of the item. Models with bidirectional attention over the item then prefill its first part without seeing the rest.

#52306 reported these splits and #52412 and #59721 fixed them, but this path remained.

## Claims

- When a cache hit ends inside a multimodal item, the request waits for a step that can schedule the rest of the item.
- Adds tests for a cache hit inside an image, at the scheduler and end to end.

## Validation

On base `51c6dfd8c`:

```text
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k mm_input_chunking                                   # CPU
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_mm_prefix_lm.py -k cache_hit_inside_image      # L4
```

With the original `scheduler.py`, three of the new checks fail: the request that hit the cache is scheduled 39 tokens into the image, the guard returns 500 tokens for a chunk that starts inside the item, and end to end the 40 image tokens prefilled first differ from the request run alone (320 / 800 elements, max abs diff 8.5e-3). With the fix, all pass.

## Details

Root cause: the guard assumes a chunk never starts inside an item, which does not hold in these cases:

- The same image is followed by a different question. The last block of the image also holds the start of the question, so that block misses and the hit stops inside the image.
- The KV cache runs short. Blocks are reused tail first, so the hit can stop early in the image, leaving most of it.

With the flag on, startup checks that one item fits in a step (`max_num_batched_tokens`), so the request is not starved. A `long_prefill_token_threshold` smaller than the item stalls it, as it already does on main (#62031, #62030).

#62782 changes the same lines; the two combine in either merge order.

No open issue or PR covers this case (checked 2026-11-02).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for investigation, implementation, tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

I found it as a numerical mismatch while porting a model with bidirectional attention over the image ([GIT](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/git)) from HF Transformers, with a small `max_num_batched_tokens` I used for testing, and opened this PR after seeing the same drift on `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it`.          "Gemma3 mm-prefix-LM image prefill hidden states should be close to HF; "
         f"got {image_cos=}"
     )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+def test_mm_prefix_lm_cache_hit_inside_image(
+    vllm_runner: type[VllmRunner],
+    image_assets: ImageTestAssets,
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+):
+    """A prefix cache hit can end inside an image. The rest of the image must
+    still be prefilled in one step, or its first part misses the rest."""
+    # One process, so that all requests of a generate() call share a step.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION", "1")
+    # Triton attention uses TF32 for fp32 by default.
+    monkeypatch.setenv("TRITON_F32_DEFAULT", "ieee")
+    # The image tokens span [100, 356), so a two-block hit ends inside it.
+    prompt = {
+        "prompt": "<bos><start_of_turn>user\n"
+        + "word " * 92
+        + "<start_of_image>What color is it?<end_of_turn>\n<start_of_turn>model\n",
+        "multi_modal_data": {"image": image_assets[0].pil_image},
+    }
+
+    def image_after_hit(vllm_model: VllmRunner) -> torch.Tensor:
+        hidden = vllm_model.apply_model(_pop_recorded_hidden_states)[0]
+        return torch.stack([hidden[position] for position in range(256, 356)])
+
+    with vllm_runner(
+        TINY_MODEL,
+        dtype="float32",
+        block_size=128,
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        enable_chunked_prefill=True,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=512,
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        disable_chunked_mm_input=True,
+        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
+    ) as vllm_model:
+        llm = vllm_model.get_llm()
+        vllm_model.apply_model(_record_hidden_states)
+
+        # Prefilled in one step; caches the first two blocks for the hit below.
+        alone = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, skip_reading_prefix_cache=True)
+        llm.generate([prompt], alone)
+        expected = image_after_hit(vllm_model)
+
+        # Text-only requests below position 256 leave 40 tokens of budget for
+        # the 112 after the hit.
+        fillers = [{"prompt_token_ids": [10 + i] * 118} for i in range(4)]
+        output = llm.generate([*fillers, prompt], SamplingParams(max_tokens=1))[-1]
+        assert output.num_cached_tokens == 256
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(image_after_hit(vllm_model), expected)

+    """A prefix cache hit can end inside a multimodal item (hits are block
+    aligned). The rest of the item must then be scheduled in one step too."""
+    block_size = 256
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        model="llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf",
+        max_num_batched_tokens=600,
+        disable_chunked_mm_input=True,
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_model_len=2048,
+    )
+
+    def image_request(req_id: str) -> Request:
+        return create_requests(
+            num_requests=1,
+            num_tokens=590,
+            mm_hashes_list=[["image"]],
+            mm_positions=[[PlaceholderRange(offset=0, length=576)]],
+            block_size=block_size,
+            req_ids=[req_id],
+        )[0]
+
+    def step() -> dict[str, int]:
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+        scheduler.update_from_output(output, make_output(scheduler))

Do you have an e2e example that triggers this issue? I am not aware of anyone actually disabling chunked mm inputs except for debugging or research purposes.

Thanks for taking a look! Yes, `test_mm_prefix_lm_cache_hit_inside_image` reproduces it end to end (see Validation). As for the flag, CUDA and ROCm turn `disable_chunked_mm_input` on automatically for models with bidirectional attention over multimodal items (Gemma3, PaliGemma, Molmo2, ...), so as far as I can tell it is on in any GPU deployment of them.

Thanks, I missed that. Are there particular bug reports that you could point to where this issue actually becomes a problem in production (e.g. requests hanging) under the settings you mentioned? Don't only rely on unit tests which might fail to capture the real behavior.

Thanks for the kind follow-up! There is no specific bug report from production that I know of. I found it as a numerical mismatch while porting a model with bidirectional attention over the image ([GIT](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/git)) from HF Transformers, with a small `max_num_batched_tokens` I used for testing, and opened this PR after seeing the same drift on `unsloth/gemma-3-4b-it`. That said, it only happens when very little budget is left in the step, and even then the tokens prefilled early miss only the few image tokens that did not fit (at most 15 with the default block size), so the effect seems small: in my samples the logprobs drifted by around 1e-2, not enough to change greedy outputs.
